title: Senior Forward Deployed Engineer (10570) Toronto, Canada
description:
Over 50,000 customers globally trust our end-to-end, cloud-driven networking solutions. They rely on our top-rated services and support to accelerate their digital transformation efforts and deliver unprecedented progress.
Become part of something big with Extreme! As a global networking leader, learn why there is no better time to join the Extreme team.
Position details
Title of position:  Senior Forward Deployed Engineer
Position type: Full time - Hybrid
Location:  Toronto, Canada
Position reports to: Director of Software Systems Engineering
Application deadline: Applications are being accepted on a rolling basis and this posting will remain open until filled.
Work authorization: We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment visa, including H-1B visas, at this time 
Scope
Are you energized by solving complex, high-impact problems directly with customers? Do you want to turn emerging technologies in intelligent networking, generative AI, agentic systems, automation, and cloud platforms into production solutions? Do you want what you build and learn in the field to help shape capabilities that benefit customers at scale?
Then come advance with us.
About the Position
Forward Deployed Engineers at Extreme are software engineers who work directly with strategic customers to jointly design, build, validate, and deploy solutions to complex business and technical problems using Extreme's products and platforms.
FDEs operate in real customer environments and own technical outcomes from discovery and solution design through implementation, deployment, and production readiness. The solutions they build must meet demanding requirements for scalability, security, reliability, observability, and operational safety.
This is a deeply technical and hands-on engineering organization. FDEs work directly with customers to understand complex problems and design, build, deploy, and stabilize production solutions using Extreme's products and platforms. They write production software, solve complex systems and integration problems, and own technical outcomes from solution design through production readiness. FDEs also identify platform gaps and define new feature requirements, working with Product teams to incorporate recurring customer needs into Extreme's products and platforms.
About the Role
As a Senior Forward Deployed Engineer, you will work directly with customer technical teams to design, build, deploy, and stabilize production solutions using Extreme's products and platforms.
You will take ownership of significant engineering workstreams and, depending on the engagement, complete customer solutions. You will work across application development, agentic AI, integrations, data, APIs, automation, networking, and cloud infrastructure to solve problems in real customer environments.
You will write production software, troubleshoot complex systems, and work through ambiguity without requiring a fully defined technical specification. You will also help identify reusable engineering patterns and platform gaps based on what you learn while delivering customer solutions.

title: Sales Ops Manager, Partners & Specialists Planning
description:
At Snowflake, we are powering the era of the agentic enterprise. To usher in this new era, we seek AI-native thinkers across every function who are energized by the opportunity to reinvent how they work. You don’t just use tools; you possess an innate curiosity, treating AI as a high-trust collaborator that is core to how you solve problems and accelerate your impact. We look for low-ego individuals who thrive in dynamic and fast-moving environments and move with an experimental mindset - who rapidly test emerging capabilities to discover simpler, more powerful ways to deliver results. At Snowflake, your role isn't just to execute a function, but to help redefine the future of how work gets done.

Snowflake's Revenue Operations team is hiring a Sales Ops Manager to own planning operations for our Partner and Product Specialist organizations. In this role, you'll run complex planning workstreams end to end, including territory design, quota setting, capacity planning, and in-year quota management. You'll be the trusted expert that Partner and Specialist leaders come to for methodology, tradeoffs, and decisions. At Snowflake, we are powering the era of the agentic enterprise and we are building an AI-native planning organization. That means AI does the analysis and production work, and you own the judgment and decisions. You'll be expected to turn your expertise into reusable skills, self-service tools, and automated workflows that grow the team's impact.

IN THIS ROLE YOU WILL GET TO:

- Own end-to-end delivery of territories, quotas, and compensation plans for Partner and Specialist organizations across all geographies, and drive alignment with Finance, Commissions, HR, and Field Ops.

- Define and govern global policies for account moves, quota changes, and in-year adjustments, including the methodology, guardrails, documentation, and change management behind them.

- Lead quota and attainment reviews across global Partner and Specialist teams. You'll find root causes, surface tradeoffs, and drive resolution with senior stakeholders.

- Anticipate how changes affect the field, Commissions, reporting, and systems, and design scalable solutions instead of one-time fixes.

- Translate business requirements into process, data, and tooling changes in Pigment, Salesforce, and Snowflake.

- Design workflows that produce decision-ready outputs, with methodology, confidence levels, and edge cases surfaced and validation built in from the start.

- Encode institutional knowledge, such as quota methodology, territory logic, and planning rules, in versioned skills and documentation that capture the why along with the how.

- Build and maintain production AI skills that encode planning methodology, validation logic, and recurring analysis for your domain. If a task runs more than twice, it should be a skill.

- Lead small cross-functional project teams, present recommendations to senior leadership, and drive decisions forward.

ON DAY ONE WE WILL EXPECT YOU TO HAVE:

- 6 to 8+ years of experience in GTM strategy, planning, or sales operations, ideally at a high-growth enterprise technology company.

- A track record of owning complex planning workstreams end to end, such as territory design, quota setting, capacity modeling, or compensation operations.

- Experience solving ambiguous, cross-functional problems where the path isn't defined, especially during periods of rapid growth.

- Strong influence skills with senior stakeholders, including the ability to frame tradeoffs clearly and move a group to a decision.

- Hands-on experience building automated or AI-assisted workflows, such as scripts, bots, AI skills, or self-service tools, that replaced manual work, with the results to show for it (hours saved, errors caught, cycles shortened).

- Deep experience with Salesforce and sales planning platforms such as Pigment or Anaplan.

- A bachelor's degree in business, statistics, economics, or another quantitative field. An MBA is a plus.

title: Customer Experience Specialist
description:
Anticipated Start Date - November 30th, 2026
Who We Are
Spot & Tango is a pet health & wellness brand on a mission to make mealtime better for dogs, and life simpler for the people who love them. Our recipes are developed by leading animal nutritionists, and are made with only real, human-grade ingredients... and nothing artificial. Through UnKibble™ and our original fresh-frozen line, we’re rethinking what feeding your dog well can look like, one bowl at a time. Since our founding in 2018, we have served over 200 million meals to happy pets across the US and Canada.
We’re a team of builders, problem solvers and dog people, united by the belief that dogs deserve better. We’re looking for people who want to do the best work of their career, dig into challenges with smart people, and help shape a brand that’s redefining an entire category. This is a chance to join a high-growth e-commerce company and have an outsized impact in a fast-paced, ambitious environment. Plus, you get to think about dogs all day.
Who You Are
The CX Specialist is a key role within our CX team, that will focus on handling sensitive and complex interactions and piloting new efforts to drive sales and retention. It's an exciting opportunity for a customer service professional to help shape the future of our CX strategy and make a significant impact on our company's growth and success.
As a CX Specialist at Spot & Tango, you'll create effortless experiences for everyone who reaches out to our team through timely, attentive, and authentic interactions. Your ability to connect with our customers, understand their unique needs, and provide meaningful solutions will shape relationships between Spot & Tango and our customers. You'll also work closely with other departments to advocate for improvements to the overall customer experience, and be the eyes and ears of the brand.
Responsibilities

• Deliver personalized and effortless interactions through inbound and outbound phone contacts, SMS, email, and chat conversations. Build a strong rapport with customers and maintain positive and professional relationships

• Become an expert in our products, services, and internal systems to provide efficient and effective support to customers

• Share insights from customer interactions with your colleagues including CX Managers and other cross-functional leaders; advocating for changes to improve our service, streamline our processes, and better serve our customers

Qualifications

• A minimum of 1 year of experience in a contact or call center, or a related field; experience working with D2C subscription businesses or in the pet industry is a plus

• Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal, and a high level of comfort in engaging with customers over the phone

• A knack for building rapport with people quickly and easily

• Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to think on your feet

• Proven ability to de-escalate and transform unhappy customers into satisfied advocates

• Eager to learn, grow, and develop your professional skills

• Resilience and a positive attitude to overcome the daily challenges that come with a customer-facing role

• The ability to thrive in a fast-paced environment and balance multiple priorities

• Believe in customer service as a growth driver and brand differentiator

• Dog lover a plus!

This opportunity is a full-time role of 40 hours per week, with a market-competitive hourly compensation and benefits package.
Weekend staffing may be required.
If you've previously applied for an earlier hiring class and are still interested, please apply again!
Spot & Tango is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

title: Program Manager
description:
Trilogy Federal drives innovative solutions for complex business challenges across financial management, healthcare, and government industries. Our collaborative, client-first service approach, combined with our commitment to the rapid implementation of pragmatic solutions, has earned Trilogy an unparalleled reputation for delivering transformative results.
The Program Manager will serve as the senior contractor leader accountable for successful execution of the nationwide Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Transition Assistance Program (TAP), including service delivery across more than 300 installations and oversight of a geographically dispersed Benefits Advisor workforce of approximately 250-280 personnel. The Program Manager will provide executive leadership across operations, curriculum, training, analytics, modernization, quality, staffing, cost, schedule, risk, and Government stakeholder coordination.

The VA Transition Assistance Program (TAP) helps transitioning Service members and their families understand and access the VA benefits, services, and resources available to them as they transition from military to civilian life. VA delivers TAP services at more than 300 military installations across the Continental United States (CONUS) and areas Outside the Continental United States (OCONUS) through a network of Benefits Advisors, supported by standardized curriculum, training, program operations, and performance management. The program is part of the broader interagency Transition Assistance Program delivered in partnership with the Department of War, Department of Labor, and other Federal agencies.

Please note that this position is contingent upon award (estimated December 2026). We expect this role to be remote, but periodic travel may be required to support program activities, customer meetings, and operations at U.S. and overseas locations. Travel frequency will vary based on program needs.

• Provide overall leadership and accountability for program performance, staffing, schedule, cost, quality, risk, and contract compliance.

title: Analyst, Demand & Supply Planning

We're building the platform they run on, and a brand they'll be proud to be part of.

Confido is the AI operating system that runs cash application, deductions, trade and planning in one place for CPG brands. That means Finance, Sales, and Ops finally work on the same number.

We’re trusted by 250+ brands managing $30B+ in revenue, including Daisy, OLIPOP, Simple Mills, Idahoan, and more. We've achieved best-in-class growth and recently raised a $55M Series B led by Insight Partners to accelerate our momentum.

We're seeking a hands-on planning professional from the CPG world to join us as an Analyst for our demand and supply planning modules. You'll own getting customers live on Confido, translating how their planning teams actually operate into a working setup on our platform. This role is highly executional: you'll be in the details of customer data, planning parameters, and workflows every day, making sure implementations land on time and deliver real value. title: Licensed Telehealth Therapist / Mental Health Counselor (Virginia)
description:
Prosper Health is on a mission to make life happier and healthier for autistic and neurodivergent adults.

Despite autism diagnoses increasing more than 5x in the past 25 years, autistic adults have been systematically overlooked. This has led to extremely poor outcomes, including high rates of co-occurring mental health conditions and a lower life expectancy. Prosper is here to change that.

We deliver specialized mental health services for autistic adults, covered by insurance. We've helped tens of thousands of people receive an autism diagnosis for the first time, work with neurodivergent-affirming therapists, and find belonging through community. Our outcomes meaningfully outperform traditional care for autistic adults, with substantially greater improvements in mood, anxiety, and quality of life.

Prosper is growing 3x year over year and are at mid-double-digit millions in run-rate revenue, with thousands of active clients and 400+ clinicians. We're a high-ownership, mission-driven team, building something that has never existed for autistic and neurodivergent adults.

We're hiring Licensed Mental Health Therapists (LCSW, LPC, LMHC) to provide therapy for autistic and neurodivergent adults via telehealth. You'll join a team dedicated to creating affirming, accessible mental health services for the neurodivergent community.
Our clinicians come from diverse backgrounds and career stages - whether you're passionate about neurodiversity advocacy, seeking flexibility and better work-life balance, or looking to add specialized experience to your existing practice, we offer roles to match your professional goals.

As Flow Lead / Central Flow Lead, you will serve as the central command point for labor allocation and operational flow across our Fulfillment Centers in Germany. Operating from your desk, you will monitor real-time operational performance, dynamically allocate workforce capacity, and coordinate with on-site teams to keep every site running at peak efficiency.

Your mission is simple: turn live data into immediate action. By anticipating bottlenecks, balancing labor across sectors, and keeping operations aligned, you’ll ensure every order is processed seamlessly and delivered on time.

WHY THIS ROLE IS EXCITING

- Impact at scale: Directly influence labor allocation and operational output across Germany’s Fulfillment Centers from a single, centralized control tower.

- Real-time decision-making: Work in a dynamic environment where live data translates directly into high-impact operational adjustments.

- Smart logistics & tech: Drive performance at the intersection of automation, WMS platforms, and data-driven workforce management.

- True ownership: Anticipate disruptions, resolve bottlenecks early, and maintain optimal operational flow under pressure.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

- Control the flow: Monitor real-time dashboards and direct automated labor flow by assigning team members across individual sectors through central control tools.

- Balance capacity dynamically: Adjust workforce distribution and shift plans on the fly in response to fluctuating order volumes and site priorities.

- Drive operational KPIs: Track CPT (Critical Pull Time), SLAs, idle time, and sector efficiency-identifying bottlenecks early and executing timely interventions.

- Keep teams aligned: Partner closely with Area Managers, Operations Managers, and on-site shop floor teams to execute adjustments and maintain consistent operational standards.

- Optimize continuously: Analyze shift performance, identify recurring process gaps, review SOP compliance with site teams, and contribute feedback for next-generation labor management tools.

- Relevant operational background: Experience in dispatch, logistics, operational planning, supply chain, e-commerce, or fulfillment (experience with automated warehouses or labor scheduling is a plus).

- Control-tower mindset: Strong ability to connect the dots across complex, fast-paced operations and make confident, data-driven decisions under pressure.

- Tech confidence: Comfortable steering operations using real-time dashboards, WMS platforms, and automated labor allocation tools.

- Strong language & communication skills: Very good English for daily operations and reporting, combined with strong Romanian language skills for direct, clear coordination with shop floor teams.

- Shift availability: Willingness to work in a 3-shift system from Monday to Friday.

- Structured & proactive approach: A problem-solver who anticipates disruptions rather than just reacting to them.

WHAT WE OFFER ON TOP OF YOUR BASE SALARY

- Daily meal allowance: An additional €9.00 tax-free meal allowance for every working day

- Daily travel allowance: An additional €5.00 daily subsidy toward your commuting costs

- Semi-annual vouchers: €300.00 in vouchers issued twice a year (€600 total annually)

- Knuspr Xtra Account: 10% cashback on your orders returned directly as Knuspr credits

- CorporateBenefits perks: Great discounts on fitness, travel, event tickets, shopping, and more

title: Programmatic EHS Manager - Low Voltage Deployment
description:
About the Role
We're looking for a Programmatic EHS Manager to create, train, implement, and manage Nscale 's overall Environmental, Health & Safety program for Low Voltage. You'll set the safety standards, processes, and metrics that every low-voltage project follows, and make sure they are applied consistently across sites and regions as we scale AI data center deployments.
The program covers everyone doing low-voltage work for Nscale : our full-time employees, Nscale contract employees, and the installation contractors we hire. You'll own the program for Nscale 's own workforce and manage how installation contractors' safety programs meet our standards.
Confined space entry is a major part of this role. Low-voltage work regularly takes crews into underground vaults, manholes, utility tunnels, duct banks, and other permit-required spaces, and you will make sure everyone who enters them is trained, permitted, monitored, and covered by a rescue plan.
Our sites run several safety programs at once, including the general contractor's, the site owner's, and Nscale 's own. You'll be the low-voltage team's main EHS contact with all of them. This is a program role rather than a site role, but in rare cases you will cover site safety directly when there is a gap in coverage.
What You'll Do
EHS Program Ownership

• Create, implement, and manage Nscale 's EHS program for Low Voltage, including policies, standards, procedures, and site-specific safety plans.

• Define program requirements for job hazard analyses (JHAs), pre-task planning, permits to work, and stop-work authority.

• Set standards for high-risk activities common to low-voltage work, including confined space entry, work at heights, ladders and mobile elevated work platforms (MEWPs), work near energized equipment, lockout/tagout (LOTO), core drilling and dust control, firestopping, fiber optic handling, and material handling of cable reels and trays.

• Ensure the program complies with OSHA (29 CFR 1910 and 1926, including Subpart AA for confined spaces), NFPA 70E, state requirements, and site owner and customer rules.

Training & Safety Culture

• Build and deliver the low-voltage safety training program for Nscale full-time employees, contract employees, and installation contractors.

• Confined space entry: train and verify competency for entrants, attendants, and entry supervisors before any entry, covering permits, atmospheric testing and continuous monitoring, ventilation, isolation, and communication.

• Confined space entry: ensure every entry has a written rescue plan, with rescue services that are trained, available, and able to respond in time, and audit entries in the field.

• Develop and deliver training on program standards, hazard recognition, and other high-risk work.

• Maintain training and competency records for all low-voltage personnel.

• Build a strong reporting culture where near misses and hazards are raised early and stop-work authority is used without hesitation.

Workforce & Contractor Safety Management

• Manage safety for Nscale full-time and contract employees, including onboarding, PPE, required certifications, and fitness for high-risk tasks.

• Review and approve installation contractors' safety programs, safety plans, and training records before mobilization.

• Own contractor safety prequalification and onboarding requirements, working with Procurement and project managers.

• Track contractor safety performance and drive corrective actions or escalation when expectations are not met.

Site Safety Program Integration

• Serve as the low-voltage team's EHS point of contact with the general contractor, site owner, and other trade safety programs on each site.

• Align low-voltage safety plans with the general contractor's site-specific safety plan, permit systems (confined space, hot work, LOTO, energized work), and orientation requirements.

• Attend general contractor safety meetings and bring site-wide requirements back to low-voltage c

description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today, SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of making life multiplanetary and expanding consciousness to the stars.

SpaceXSI is building Super Intelligence to help humanity understand the universe. Our teams are building the full Super Intelligence stack: from our Colossus supercomputers, to Grok models, to our suite of applications, including Grok Bot, Grok Build, Grok Imagine, Grok Voice, and X. We're creating a powerful flywheel where more compute trains better models, better models power more useful products, and what we learn from people using those products shapes what we build next.

About the role

Lifecycle Growth's job is to get more people using Grok, Grok Bot, X, Cursor and the API every day, and to turn that use into revenue. We own everything after signup: getting people to value, converting them to paid, growing their teams and keeping them coming back. We do it with lifecycle marketing, in-product messaging and a steady stream of experiments, and much of the work runs on agents we build ourselves.

This isn't a traditional marketing role. You'll do the work of a product manager, a product marketer and a marketing engineer, often in the same day. You'll own lifecycle growth for one or more of our products. You'll figure out where the biggest opportunity is, design the program, build it and show whether it actually moved the number.

The job spans consumer and business, self-serve and sales-led, so you'll need to think as clearly about a solo user's first week as about a team's path to an enterprise deal. You'll go deep on the systems underneath, like who's eligible, what triggers a message, how events and attributes are modeled, and how data moves from the warehouse into our messaging tools. When the best fix lives in the product or the data, you'll make the case and either build it yourself or work with engineering to ship it.

This is an in-person role based in our San Francisco office.

- Data and audiences: Use SQL and product data to size opportunities, build the audiences and triggers behind each program, and prove what actually drove revenue.

- Journeys: Architect multi-step, cross-channel programs across email, push and in-app, with event-based triggers, branching and suppression logic, and personalization drawn from product usage, plan and billing state, and company and role enrichment.

- Systems: Drive and continuously improve the data model lifecycle runs on, including identity, events, attributes and eligibility, and partner with engineering on the warehouse syncs, APIs and webhooks that keep it accurate in real time.

- Measurement: Run every program as an experiment with a proper holdout, measure incremental lift, and make judgment calls when a result is inconclusive.

- Portfolio: Manage lifecycle as a portfolio of programs, putting more behind what works and retiring what doesn't.

- In-product: Own in-product messaging and experiments, from onboarding and upgrade prompts to post-purchase plan tours, and partner with product and engineering to improve our in-app comms systems.

- Tooling: Use code and agents to build the internal tools, templates and automated QA the team runs on, so each new program ships faster than the last.

- 8+ years in Lifecycle, Growth PMM or Product Growth at a high-growth product company.

We're hiring a Senior Developer with deep mobile expertise for a small, self-contained innovation group (Initial three-month contract, with opportunity for extension or move to full-time). Working alongside a Product Manager and a web-focused developer, you will take an ambiguous business problem, turn it into a testable product bet, and build the smallest end-to-end experience that can generate meaningful evidence, often in roughly one to two weeks. You will bring early versions back to customers and the market validation group, gather feedback, and rapidly iterate through V1, V2, V3, and beyond. Once the concept is validated, the group will shift from proving the idea to determining what must change for it to become secure, reliable, scalable, and ready for handoff.
The group operates like an entrepreneurial startup within the larger organization and owns the path from problem discovery through rapid prototyping, customer and market validation, iterative development, and a validated proof of concept. From there, it determines what is required to harden and scale the product before handing it to the core product and engineering team.
The operating principle is simple: build to learn first, then build to scale. During validation, speed comes from controlling scope and making deliberate, reversible technical choices-not from designing the final production architecture before the opportunity is proven. Security, privacy, and responsible data handling remain non-negotiable throughout. Once an idea demonstrates value, you will work with our Core team at key technical integration points to harden, refactor, or redesign what is needed for scale. That judgment lets us discard weak ideas cheaply and invest deeply in the ones that earn it.
This is a fit for someone with strong product and commercial instincts, sound technical judgment, and a high degree of ownership. You identify gaps, propose a path forward, and keep momentum without waiting for perfect requirements. You own outcomes, make clear trade-offs to meet timelines, and raise consequential risks early.
What you'll do:

• Work with the Project Lead, Product Manager and Web Developer to turn ambiguous problems into unified driver-and-admin experiences

• Build within the shared codebase, behind feature flags and in isolated modules that can be removed cleanly

• Once a concept is validated, identify and complete the work required to harden, scale, test, and release it

• Prepare validated features and technical context for a clean handoff to the core product and engineering team

Core Experience

• 6-8 years as a software engineer at a senior level, with a track record of product work at startups and in fast-paced environments

• You've built from nothing, cut scope under time pressure, and ship

title: Strategy Principal, Office of the COO
description:
Strategy Principal, Office of the COO
Chief of Staff-level role | Walnut Insurance | Remote, Canada | Partner to the COO and CPO
The role
You'll be the operating and strategy partner to our COO and CPO. Half the job is the work a top strategy consultant does for a client: help decision, size the opportunity, build the case, pressure-test the plan, write the recommendation. The other half is what a good chief of staff does: turn that decision into execution, so momentum never depends on two people's calendars. You'll work across sales, product and partnerships as we grow in Canada and the US, in a regulated industry where banks, telcos, lenders and insurers are the buyers. And you'll do it with an AI-native toolkit that lets one person deliver what used to take a team.
About Walnut
Walnut is Canada's leading embedded insurance platform. Partners like Wealthsimple, BMO, KOHO and TELUS use us to launch insurance inside their products in 90 days, compared with nine months or more going direct to a carrier. We hold the carrier relationships, the licences and the compliance; our partners keep the customer.
Non-negotiable: you build with AI every day
You've done strategy work to a top-tier standard, in financial services. Maybe that was at a leading consultancy, in a bank or insurer's strategy or corporate development group, at a fintech or insurtech, or in a founder's office doing the same job without the title. You know how a bank, a carrier and an enterprise buyer make decisions, and how long they take. You can read a partner's P&L, a loss ratio and a take rate and tell us whether a program will make money. And you can write a board-grade recommendation on one page.
AI is how you already work, not a tool you'll pick up here. You build agents, Claude Skills and automated workflows as a daily habit, connect them to live systems like HubSpot, Slack and email through APIs and MCP, and can show us what you've built and the impact it had. If you use AI only for drafting and summarizing, this isn't the role.
What you'll do

• Run strategy the way a consultant would. Own the thinking behind our biggest calls: which markets and channels come first, how we price a program, which partners we chase and which we pass on, what a carrier deal is worth. Size markets from the bottom up, model partner economics, map the competition, and bring the COO and CPO options with a recommendation, the trade-offs and the point at which you'd change your mind. You'll run the weekly strategic review that keeps every initiative red, yellow or green.

• Make the call, or frame it. Decide what's yours to decide inside agreed guardrails, and bring the rest to the COO and CPO framed so the decision takes ten minutes. Brief them before key meetings, send recaps with decisions, owners and dates, and hand work off to named owners with clear scope.

• Own follow-through. Keep one current view of what's owed to and by the COO and CPO across partners, carriers and the team. Raise risks before they slip and push deals and projects forward between meetings.

• Shape the deals that matter. Work alongside our Sales Team on pipeline, HubSpot reporting and sales infrastructure. Build the business cases, solution outlines and proposals for enterprise deals with banks, telcos and lenders, and help us build the go-to-market in both markets.

• Build the materials. Turn notes, data and rough direction into executive, investor, partner and board decks, briefs and models, with accurate numbers and a clear point of view. You'll prepare board materials but won't attend board meetings.

• Keep one version of the facts. Maintain the roadmap, requirements and partner records, and make sure material decisions are captured in writing.

• Build our AI operating system. Design and run the Claude Skills, agents and workflows that remove manual work across the executive team. Our stack: Claude (Skills, Code, Cowork, Design, MCP), Granola, HubSpot, , Slack, Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, Figm

For more than 20 years, Gabriele Consulting Group Inc. Industry: Construction / Hotel Renovations
Working Hours: US Business Hours (3pm to 11pm SA hours)
Position Overview
We are looking for a driven and results-focused Sales Consultant to join a growing construction company specialising in renovation and improvement projects for hotels and hospitality properties.
The successful candidate will be responsible for proactively identifying hotel opportunities, building relationships with key decision-makers, and generating new renovation projects through consistent outbound sales and cold calling .
This is a highly proactive sales role suited to someone who is confident on the phone, comfortable speaking with senior decision-makers, and motivated by targets and winning new business. If you enjoy turning a cold call into a genuine business opportunity, this could be a great fit!
Key Responsibilities

• Conduct a high volume of daily outbound cold calls to hotels and hospitality businesses.

• Identify hotels that may require renovations, upgrades, repairs, refurbishments, or improvement projects.

• Research hotels and identify relevant decision-makers, including General Managers, Property Managers, Directors of Operations, and Facilities Managers.

• Introduce the company's construction and renovation services in a professional and compelling manner.

• Build and maintain relationships with hotel decision-makers and key contacts.

• Qualify leads by understanding the hotel's current and upcoming renovation requirements.

• Generate qualified leads and schedule appointments or consultations for the construction team.

• Follow up consistently with prospects through phone calls, email, and other communication channels.

• Maintain accurate records of calls, leads, conversations, follow-ups, and opportunities within the CRM.

• Develop a strong pipeline of potential hotel renovation projects.

• Meet or exceed agreed daily, weekly, and monthly activity and sales targets .

• Stay informed about the hospitality and construction markets to identify potential opportunities.

• Work closely with the internal construction and estimating teams to ensure qualified opportunities are properly handed over.

Requirements

• Proven experience in B2B sales, business development, telemarketing, or lead generation .

• Strong cold-calling experience, preferably within construction, property, hospitality, facilities management, or a related industry.

• A confident and professional telephone manner.

• Excellent verbal and written communication skills.

• Comfortable speaking with business owners, General Managers, and senior-level decision-makers.

• Highly persistent and comfortable handling rejection - because unfortunately, "no thanks" is going to make an appearance or two!

• Strong follow-up and relationship-building skills.

• Ability to work independently and manage a high-volume outbound sales pipeline.

• Target-driven with a strong focus on achieving measurable results.

• Excellent organisational and time-management skills.

title: Thermal Engineer
description:
COMPANY

NewOrbit builds satellites that fly in very low Earth orbit, below 300 km, along with the electric propulsion that keeps them there.

Flying closer to Earth means sharper imagery from smaller optics, and an orbit that cleans itself: our satellites de-orbit within a month at end of life, leaving no debris.

Our AURA family of RF gridded ion thrusters powers our own NEO-1 satellite, with first flight planned for Q3 2028, and is also offered to other operators.

Electric propulsion is what lets our satellites hold very low orbits, and our AURA RF gridded ion thruster is at the centre of it.

Role

We are looking for a skilled Thermal Engineer with experience in spacecraft thermal management at both the subsystem and spacecraft level.

You’ll work closely with a cross-functional team - including mechanical, propulsion, electronics, and mission planning - to ensure reliable thermal performance of our satellite throughout all mission phases: from launch to operation in orbit and end-of-life.

You should be capable of delivering a thermal control system from scratch and taking full ownership of it, ensuring the success of our mission.

Key Responsibilities

- Perform steady-state and transient thermal analysis of the spacecraft across all mission phases (TVAC testing, launch, orbit).

- Model and validate heat management strategies in the harsh environment of vacuum, where conduction and radiation are dominant

- Identify and manage worst-case scenarios in extreme thermal conditions (both hot and cold), accounting for on-orbit environmental factors and internal power dissipation

- Design and implement thermal control solutions such as multilayer insulation (MLI), radiators, heaters, thermo-optical coatings, thermistors, and thermal straps

- Develop and support thermal vacuum (TVAC) test procedures, instrumentation setup, and post-test data analysis.

- Be hands on in hardware testing for validation of processes, instrumentation, and materials and components chosen for in house developments

Fundamental Requirements

- Solid understanding of thermal engineering principles in the context of spacecraft systems.

- Hands-on experience with thermal simulation tools such as Systema, Thermal Desktop, ESATAN, or equivalent.

- Experience with environmental and lab testing (TVAC, thermal cycling, AIT process
validation).

- Comfortable working in a fast-paced, iterative development environment.

Nice-to-Haves

- Experience designing or testing spacecraft thermal systems.

- Exposure to multidisciplinary space system development or mission analysis.

WHY NEWORBIT SPACE?

- Pioneering space technology - Your work on our RF gridded ion thrusters and VLEO satellite platform will redefine satellite operations and challenge traditional LEO.

- Ownership and impact - You'll have a level of ownership that's rare in the space industry, and you'll take part in the full lifecycle of satellite technology.

- Equity and competitive salary - Alongside a competitive salary you receive a company ownership stake, so you share in the technology you help build and in our collective success.

- Comprehensive benefits - Private health insurance with dental and optical cover, and annual health check-ups.

- Hybrid working - One dedicated remote day per week.

- Visa sponsorship and relocation support - We sponsor visas and provide relocation support for candidates moving to join us.

MniMed is seeking an experienced Sr. Principal Field Clinical Research Specialist to support and lead clinical research initiatives, ensuring high-quality clinical data and compliance with applicable regulatory requirements. This role will collaborate cross-functionally with clinical, medical, and research teams to support study execution, site management, and overall clinical trial success. The position is fully remote and open to candidates anywhere in the United States, with travel required as needed to support clinical study activities. About Tailscale

Tailscale is making safe connection effortless by delivering software that makes it easy to securely interconnect people and their devices, no matter where they are. From hobbyists to multinational corporations, teams of every size use Tailscale each day to protect their networks, share access to internal tools, and more. About the Role
We're looking for an Integrated ABM Campaign Manager to develop and scale creative, targeted campaigns that engage priority accounts and drive pipeline across our Enterprise and Mid-Market segments.
You'll own the strategy and execution of 1:1 and 1:few ABM campaigns, bringing together paid advertising, personalized content, direct mail, gifting, and coordinated Sales outreach to reach the right people at the right accounts.

You'll also partner closely with our wider ABM, Sales, and Partner Marketing team to connect campaigns with account priorities, strategic experiences, and partner-led opportunities.
Key Responsibilities

• Own the strategy, planning, execution, and optimization of integrated ABM campaigns across Enterprise and Mid-Market audiences.

• Develop campaign audiences, messaging, channel plans, budgets, and success metrics based on Sales priorities and account insights.

• Proactively identify new campaign opportunities based on engagement signals, account intelligence, and business priorities.

• Track performance, test new approaches, and optimize for account engagement, meetings, pipeline creation, and progression.

What We Are Looking For

• 5+ years of B2B marketing experience, with a background in building ABM campaigns for both net-new acquisition and customer expansion.

• Hands-on experience with LinkedIn advertising, audience segmentation, and marketing automation.

• Comfortable working with data, testing new ideas, and using performance insights to improve results.

• Familiarity with Salesforce, HubSpot, LinkedIn Campaign Manager, Clay, or Common Room.

Job Title: Grant Reviewer, K-12 Education (Direct Investment in Students)
Work Arrangement: Remote
Location: Remote, United States
Employment Type: Part-Time, Independent Contractor (1099)
Engagement Type: Short-term, per grant competition; paid per application reviewed

Position Summary
Dhaka Technologies Limited Company is hiring Grant Reviewers on behalf of the Office of the State Superintendent of Education (OSSE), the District of Columbia's state education agency, for its Direct Investment in Students grant competition. OSSE is seeking experienced K-12 education professionals who have served as grant reviewers for OSSE in the past.
Grant reviewers provide independent subject matter expertise to read, score, and comment on competitive grant applications submitted by local education agencies, schools, community-based organizations, and other eligible entities. All reviews are completed remotely in OSSE's online Enterprise Grants Management System (EGMS), and reviewer scores are used to recommend applications for funding. OSSE selects reviewers from the qualified pool and gives preference to reviewers who have satisfactorily completed reviews for its competitions in previous years.
Work Schedule
This is a remote, part-time assignment. Reviews are completed on your own schedule within each deadline. The approximate commitment for this competition is:

• Orientation and EGMS training: a virtual webinar held approximately within two weeks of the engagement start date.

• Review window: usually two weeks from the date applications are assigned, unless OSSE specifies otherwise.

• Facilitated discussion (only if needed): a phone or video conference, usually about three business days after the scoring due date, held when panel scores differ significantly.

• Approximate completion of reviewer work: November 6, 2026. Final dates are confirmed before orientation.

Key Responsibilities

• Complete OSSE's EGMS training and attend the virtual, grant-specific orientation webinar before reviewing any applications.

• Independently read and conduct a detailed review of each assigned application (typically two or more per competition) as one of three reviewers on an EGMS review panel, working remotely and separately.

• Apply K-12 education expertise to assess the quality, feasibility, and expected student impact of each applicant's proposed activities.

• Complete a fully scored rubric for every section of each application, applying the established scoring criteria consistently and objectively.

• Write clear, constructive comments describing strengths and weaknesses that justify and align with the scores given. Reviews may be shared with applicants on request, with reviewer names and contact information removed.

• Base all scores and comments only on the content of each applicant's submission in EGMS.

• Submit all scores and comments in EGMS by the review deadline, usually two weeks from receiving the applications.

• Participate in a facilitated panel discussion by phone or video conference when scores differ significantly, then submit a final rubric with updated scores and comments reflecting any changes.

• Disclose any conflict of interest with applicant organizations and do not review any application where a conflict exists.

• Direct EGMS technical questions to the EGMS manual, the resources at grants.osse.dc.gov, or the EGMS call center at (202) 719-6500, and direct questions about the grant or about scoring to OSSE grant program staff.

Required Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree or higher.

• Past service as a competitive grant reviewer for OSSE.

• Professional experience in K-12 education.

• Reliable access to a computer, the internet, and a phone.

• Availability for the full review process, including EGMS training, the orientation webinar, the complete review window, and a facilitated discussion if one is required.

• No conflict of interest with any applicant organization in this competition, confirmed t

Our Robotics team is focused on unlocking general-purpose robotics and pushing towards AGI-level intelligence in dynamic, real-world settings. Working across the entire model stack, we integrate cutting-edge hardware and software to explore a broad range of robotic form factors. We strive to seamlessly blend high-level AI capabilities with the constraints of physical systems to improve peoples’ lives.

About the Role

As a Test Engineer on the Robotics team, you will help shape the next generation of embodied AI. You’ll design and run rigorous, exploratory and requirements-driven tests-building custom test equipment, analyzing results, and translating findings into actionable insights that drive design breakthroughs and mitigate risks across hardware and software. This role offers the opportunity to directly influence how our AI scales beyond simulation, ensuring that every design, test, and iteration brings us closer to truly adaptive, versatile robotic systems.

In this role, you will:

- Design and build custom test benches to evaluate system performance under realistic operating conditions; proficient in CAD and familiar with GD&T.

- Analyze and interpret test data to identify trends, anomalies, and root causes.

- Develop and maintain comprehensive test plans that validate mechanical performance against product requirements.

- Execute validation and verification testing, capturing both quantitative and qualitative data with high fidelity.

- Author clear, actionable test reports that summarize results, highlight risks, and recommend design or process changes.

- Partner with engineering, product, and leadership teams to inform design iterations and strategic decisions.

- Design and execute compliance and regulatory testing campaigns, informing in-house vs 3rd party testing strategy

You might thrive in this role if you:

- Have strong intuition for mechanical and electromechanical systems and how they fail, degrade, or vary in real-world operation.

- Enjoy hands-on lab work designing, instrumenting, operating, and debugging test equipment and robotic hardware.

- Can turn evolving requirements and ambiguous failures into repeatable tests, trustworthy data, and clear engineering decisions.

- Balance rigorous validation, safety, and traceability with rapid hardware iteration.

- Communicate clearly across mechanical, electrical, software, controls, and manufacturing teams, and build alignment on risks and corrective actions.

Preferred Qualifications

- 7+ years of experience in hardware testing or validation, including at least 2 years working with robotics hardware components and systems.

- Bachelor’s or graduate degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechatronics, Robotics, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

- Experience designing test fixtures and stands using CAD, engineering drawings, and GD&T.

- Hands-on experience integrating sensors, instrumentation, and data acquisition (DAQ) systems, including calibration and measurement traceability.

- Experience developing automated or hardware-in-the-loop tests using Python, C/C++, or AI coding tools for test execution, data collection, and analysis.

- Experience designing reliability, accelerated life, environmental, and hardware qualification tests for robotic or electromechanical systems.

- Experience supporting EVT, DVT, PVT, pilot production, or sustaining hardware validation.

- Experience using root cause analysis, FMEA, or FEA to guide design improvements.

- Experience executing product standards compliance certification campaigns.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We are looking for a Technical Program Manager to lead programs that bring our software-defined vehicle platform from automotive into naval warships. You will own the plan for adapting a production-proven vehicle OS, middleware, and tooling stack to shipboard environments, working across Applied engineering teams, Navy program offices, shipbuilders, and integration partners. This role sits at the intersection of fast-moving commercial software and complex defense acquisition, and it calls for someone who can bring modern software delivery practices into programs that have historically moved slowly. You will work closely with subject matter experts at Applied and at our customers on a technical level to get capability onto ships and into the hands of sailors.

- Drive problem-solving and decision-making across teams to resolve technical, schedule, and contractual issues
